finding.mechanism: EntityOSBridge.run uses subprocess.run with a timeout; Python documents that timeout handling kills and waits for the already-created child before TimeoutExpired is re-raised. The existing EffectGate caught every exception and persisted FAILED, which can manufacture certainty even though an external side effect may already have occurred.
finding.counterhypothesis: Treating TimeoutExpired as an ordinary FAILED result is safe because timeout implies the child never produced external effects.
finding.falsifier: A timeout is raised only after process creation/communication has begun; therefore the counterhypothesis cannot guarantee absence of external effects.
finding.risk: false FAILED classification can permit downstream logic or operators to reason as though no effect happened, violating ClayVerse unknown-outcome and no-blind-replay contracts.

changes: EntityOSBridge raises typed EntityOSOutcomeUnknown for subprocess.TimeoutExpired
EffectGate leaves that post-start ambiguous effect PENDING instead of persisting FAILED
existing episode request identity blocks same-turn automatic re-execution
existing boot recovery converts unresolved PENDING to UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART and advances entity generation
deterministic regression test covers typed timeout, retry non-reexecution, and recovery no-replay
source_candidate.liveness_tradeoff: The affected session remains blocked on the PENDING effect until canonical recovery; this is intentional fail-closed behavior rather than a second recovery path.

bounded_local_mechanism_probe.environment: Python 3.13.5; Linux 6.18.35 x86_64 isolated local container

external_primary_evidence.python_subprocess: Python 3.14 documentation: subprocess.run timeout kills and waits for the child, then re-raises TimeoutExpired; process creation itself may be non-interruptible.
